graph.notes: SonarCloud Autoscan: code pushes to GitHub trigger a Lambda that creates analysis requests in SQS; an auto-scaled Fargate service clones and analyzes the code and pushes reports to an EC2 API, which stores them in Aurora (used as a temporary queue). Up to 150k analyses per week; around 300,000 organizations supported. Planned: move to managed Amazon Elasticsearch, replace the Aurora queue with SQS, and support compiled languages (Java, C#).

nodes.name: Developers
nodes.notes: Developers write code and push it to a GitHub repo; they later view analysis results through the UI or the API.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Captures the event triggered by a code push to GitHub, does triage and some analysis, and creates an analysis request.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queue of analysis requests. Used to level the load so the Fargate service is not overwhelmed, and as the signal for Fargate auto-scaling.

nodes.name: ECS Fargate (Autoscan analyzer)
nodes.notes: Auto-scaled Fargate service plugged into the SQS queue. Polls the queue, clones the code, and analyzes it. Uses only ephemeral storage, no external storage. Supports non-compiled languages (TypeScript, Python, etc.); Java and C# planned.

nodes.name: ECS Fargate (Compute Engine)
nodes.notes: Compute Engine. Polls the database to extract reports, computes many code quality metrics, updates the database, and writes search-optimized data to Elasticsearch.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: EC2 instance that receives analysis reports through an API and stores them in the database; also serves the UI/API users call to get results. AUTOSCALE: False, SPOT: False.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Database that stores analysis reports. Used as temporary storage / a queuing mechanism for reports, and holds the final analysis results. Plan is to replace the Aurora queue with a proper SQS queue.

nodes.name: non-aws ElasticSearch
nodes.notes: In-house Elasticsearch service (not Amazon). Stores additional shared data in an optimized format for search. Plan is to move to the managed Amazon version.
